title: Trailer
when: Launches, announcements, teasers and any film whose job is anticipation rather than explanation
rules: Three acts: a cold open (sketch signal), a rising montage of 2–4 s shots split by black type cards, a silence, the title (sketch title), then a button.
Every montage shot is a place the promise touches, drawn for this film (wires, citygrid, mast are examples): never a stock skyline reused from another film.
Cards are posters, not captions: a small lead line over one or two words that fill the frame (sketch card, sketchText LEAD and CARD), sharpening out of blur under a light sweep while they push in.
Vary the cut: a flash on the hits, a whip into a card, a hard cut on action between two moving shots. Each montage shot is shorter than the last as the title approaches.
Before the title, one beat with no voice and a single element: the silence makes the hit land. End on a button: one short line after the title, like a release date.
